specification: Open Charging Technology TOTP HTTP Authentication 1.0 (draft)
description: Server-side verification of the 'Authorization: TOTP' scheme (sections 5.3, 6.2 and 8): a verifier holding 'verifier.logins' (login -> TOTP configuration; absent optional parameters mean the verifier's own defaults) at the clock 'verifier.unixTimestampMillis' receives 'authorization' (null: no header) and answers 'accepted' (the request is authenticated as 'login'), 'rejected' (401; an unknown login is indistinguishable from a wrong token) or 'malformed' (400, or 401: a server MAY treat malformed as failed). The verifier has no TLS exporter material, so a credential claiming a channel binding is rejected, never verified as raw; no presented token is bound, so a verifier with exporter material reaches the same outcomes. The clock lies at least 10s before the end of its slot for every login, so a harness setting a live server's clock may lag that much. The whole file requires the listed capabilities; harnesses without them skip it declaratively.

vectors.description: The current token of the login's configuration.
The previous slot's token: one slot of clock skew or transmission delay.
The next slot's token: a client clock one slot ahead.
A token two slots old is outside the window - which is never widened.
A token two slots ahead is outside the window.
The previous slot under a login's own configuration (60s, 16 characters, Base32, HMAC-SHA512, a non-ASCII secret); the login contains a colon.
Two slots of 60 seconds old: the window is counted in the login's slots.
Another login, verified against its own configuration.
Another login's current token is no token of this login.
An unknown login is rejected exactly like a wrong token - with a token that is valid for a known login.
The current token under HMAC-SHA512 is no token of a login configured for HMAC-SHA256.
The first 11 characters of the current token.
The current token of length 13 - which starts with the length 12 token, as every longer token of the slot does.
The current token with the case of its first character changed: tokens are compared exactly.
The current token with a leading space inside the Base64: compared exactly, never trimmed.
The current raw token without tlscb: the default true claims a channel binding, which a verifier without exporter material rejects - never verifying the token as raw.
The same with tlscb=true spelled out.
Scheme, parameter names and the tlscb value are matched case-insensitively.
An unknown parameter is ignored.
No Authorization header at all.
The totp parameter is mandatory.
An empty token.
A valid token followed by a second totp parameter: ambiguous, so malformed - never the first one wins.
The same with the valid token last - never the last one wins.
